channel.title: Khoa Tran Engineering Portfolio
channel.description: Case studies, system design notes, and interactive engineering experiments.

item.title: Field Note: What My Own Git Log Proves About Spec-Driven Development
item.description: PFM's governance docs claim every business rule traces from spec to test to code. A plain git log, not the docs, is what actually proves it — and it also shows two honest cases of deliberately not fixing something.

item.title: The Hidden Costs of Firebase Cloud Functions
item.description: A follow-up to the field note on choosing Firebase Functions over Cloud Run: two costs the concurrency model doesn't advertise on its own.

item.title: ADR: Tracing vs Metrics for Observability in Aegis
item.description: An Architecture Decision Record on why distributed tracing and metrics answer different questions in Aegis, and which one should gate a page for what.

item.title: Database Indexing for Time-Series: B-Tree vs BRIN in PostgreSQL
item.description: Why a Block Range Index, not the default B-Tree, is the right structure for naturally time-ordered data — and why QuantAlpha's tick-ingestion pipeline hasn't needed it yet.

item.title: Gossip Protocol Visualizer: How Cluster Membership Actually Spreads
item.description: A real push-based epidemic broadcast, run and scrubbed round by round, showing why gossip converges in O(log n) rounds instead of O(n).

item.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token Bucket vs Leaky Bucket vs Fixed Window
item.description: Three rate limiting algorithms, run for real against the same burst scenario, to show what each one actually does differently — not just what it's named.

item.title: WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events: What Holding 5,000 Connections Open Actually Costs
item.description: A real harness measuring server memory for thousands of concurrent WebSocket vs SSE connections — written before the article, per the lesson from three prior benchmark rewrites.

item.title: Designing a Global API Gateway: Edge Routing Beyond a Single Aegis Instance
item.description: Aegis's GraphQL gateway solves API shape for one instance. This is the layer above it a real deployment would need once there's more than one — and why that's a different problem, not a bigger version of the same one.

item.title: The SPA Google Never Saw
item.description: This portfolio was a client-rendered SPA on GitHub Pages for months. Every deep link a crawler could find returned 404. Here's how I found it, and what I built instead of migrating frameworks.

item.title: ADR: Why Prerender Instead of Migrating to Next.js
item.description: This portfolio's original decision to build a custom JAMstack instead of using Next.js still held once a crawler-visibility bug surfaced. Here's why the fix was a build step, not a framework migration.

item.title: Field Note: A Diagram That Wouldn't Render
item.description: A sequence diagram in a new case study failed to parse. The cause wasn't the character I suspected first — and the fix I tried second broke the same way for a different reason.

item.title: Field Note: Measuring Contrast Instead of Guessing at It
item.description: A prior audit flagged 44 text-slate-400 occurrences as 'potentially borderline' and correctly refused to fix them blind. Building a real contrast checker turned that judgment call into a number — and found two unrelated bugs on the way.

item.title: PFM: A Spec-Driven, Invite-Only Personal Finance Tracker
item.description: A React 19 + Go financial tracker built spec-first: every business rule traces from an SRS to an SDS to a passing integration test, with a hard server-side boundary between the browser and the API.

item.title: Building Jujuja: A Production Quest System for Burst Traffic
item.description: How we built the Jujuja backend to handle 1,500 concurrent users per minute during campaign bursts, processing daily quests and loyalty points using BullMQ and NestJS.

item.title: Designing a Multi-Role HFT Research Platform
item.description: How I architected QuantAlpha Lab, a distributed research platform that bridges the gap between Python data science and Go backend engineering.

item.title: gRPC Service Mesh in Go: Designing the Aegis Auth Platform
item.description: A walkthrough of Aegis — a modular auth platform built on gRPC inter-service communication, a GraphQL gateway, Kafka audit logging, and full OpenTelemetry trace propagation.

item.title: ADR: Firestore vs PostgreSQL for Event Sourcing in Core Banking
item.description: An Architecture Decision Record detailing why Firestore was chosen over PostgreSQL as the primary EventStore for the Event-Driven Core Banking platform.

item.title: ADR: Choosing a GraphQL Gateway Over REST for Aegis
item.description: An Architecture Decision Record detailing why Aegis uses a GraphQL API Gateway to aggregate internal gRPC microservices instead of a traditional REST API.

item.title: Sub-300ms Store Discovery: Designing Geo-Search with Algolia
item.description: How we leveraged Algolia to build a blazing fast, geo-aware store discovery engine for SeensioGO and Jujuja, achieving 150-300ms latency.

item.title: Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry and Jaeger
item.description: A practical guide to instrumenting Go microservices with OpenTelemetry: from SDK setup to trace context propagation, sampling strategies, and reading Jaeger flame graphs.

item.title: Event Sourcing vs CRUD: When to Choose Each
item.description: A decision framework for choosing between Event Sourcing and traditional CRUD, based on building both a CRUD loyalty API and a full event-sourced core banking system.

item.title: Order Book Imbalance (OBI) as a Signal for Short-Term Price Prediction
item.description: Research notes on extracting Order Book Imbalance (OBI) features from Level-3 market data (VN30F2112) to train rolling-window ML classifiers for High-Frequency Trading.

item.title: Interactive Event Sourcing Replay
item.description: An interactive visualization of how application state is derived from an immutable, append-only event log.

item.title: Redis Streams vs BullMQ: Choosing Your Job Queue
item.description: A practical comparison of Redis Streams and BullMQ based on using both in production — covering delivery semantics, consumer group models, and failure handling patterns.

item.title: Interactive Saga State Machine Visualizer
item.description: An interactive visualization of the Saga distributed transaction pattern, demonstrating automated compensating rollbacks.

item.title: Designing a Multi-Service Auth Platform: The Aegis Architecture
item.description: A deep dive into Aegis, a high-performance authorization platform using gRPC microservices, a GraphQL gateway, Kafka audit logging, and OpenTelemetry.

item.title: Designing a Real-Time Fraud Detection Engine with Velocity Rules
item.description: How I built a real-time fraud detection engine using Event Sourcing, CQRS, and velocity rules to automatically freeze malicious accounts in a core banking system.

item.title: Implementing the Saga Pattern for Distributed Money Transfers
item.description: How I designed a Saga orchestrator pattern for two-phase distributed transfers between account aggregates, with automatic compensation and dead-letter recovery.

item.title: Field Note: Go vs TypeScript for Backend Services
item.description: A working engineer's honest comparison of Go and TypeScript for backend services, based on using both in production — and a framework for choosing between them.

item.title: Benchmark: Event Replay in PostgreSQL vs Firestore
item.description: An interactive benchmark comparing the time it takes to replay tens of thousands of immutable events into a Read Projection.

item.title: Benchmark: Go vs TypeScript Concurrency
item.description: An interactive benchmark visualizing memory footprint and execution time for handling tens of thousands of concurrent network-bound tasks.

item.title: Event-Driven Core Banking System
item.description: A core banking ledger demonstrating Event Sourcing, CQRS, and distributed Saga transfers.

item.title: Atomic Financial Transactions in a NoSQL World: Building the J-Point Loyalty Engine
item.description: Implementing virtual currency transactions on Firestore with <1% consistency errors, covering atomic operation design and edge case handling.

item.title: Designing a Burst-Traffic Async Job Pipeline: The Jujuja Quest System
item.description: How we redesigned daily quest processing from synchronous handlers to a queue-driven worker pool that handles 1,500 concurrent users during campaign windows.

item.title: Field Note: Why I Chose Firebase Functions Over Cloud Run
item.description: A practical evaluation of Firebase Functions vs Cloud Run, and why the simplest serverless model won out for our specific workloads.

item.title: Aegis: High-Performance Auth & Authorization Platform
item.description: A modular, high-performance Identity and Policy microservice platform in Go, featuring sub-5ms RBAC evaluations and distributed tracing.

item.title: Architecture Breakdown: CQRS for Mid-size Products
item.description: A practical guide to adopting CQRS for mid-size products: when it helps, when it hurts, and the pragmatic migration path.

item.title: Engineering Lessons from a Failed Rollout
item.description: What a painful rollback taught us about blast-radius control, feature flags, and building safety into the release pipeline.

item.title: System Design Notes: Idempotency
item.description: Practical patterns for making API writes replay-safe under network retries and partial distributed failures.

item.title: Designing a Permission System: Beyond Simple Roles
item.description: How to evolve from brittle role checks to a maintainable, high-performance policy-based authorization engine.

item.title: Scaling Background Jobs: Adaptive Concurrency
item.description: Operational patterns and practical lessons for scaling asynchronous jobs while keeping failure rates and costs predictable.

item.title: Queue vs Pub/Sub Comparison Notes
item.description: How delivery semantics and fan-out requirements should dictate your choice between Message Queues and Pub/Sub systems.

item.title: Throughput Simulation Notes
item.description: Experiment notes on balancing worker count and tail latency under failure pressure using client-side simulations.

item.title: Building an Event-Driven Architecture
item.description: A practical blueprint for introducing domain events to untangle a monolith without losing delivery guarantees.

item.title: System Design Trade-offs in Practice
item.description: A structured framework to communicate architecture trade-offs with product, operations, and engineering teams.

item.title: QuantAlpha: High-Frequency Trading Research Platform
item.description: A distributed research platform for High-Frequency Trading (HFT) utilizing Redis Streams for asynchronous model training and order book imbalance (OBI) analysis.
